title: Prompt Injection Attacks in Large Language Models and AI Agent Systems: A Comprehensive Review of Vulnerabilities, Attack Vectors, and Defense Mechanisms
explain_beginner: This paper examines a major security problem with AI language models: attackers can trick them into ignoring their instructions and misbehaving. As these AI systems become more integrated into real applications, new attack methods have emerged, especially through connected tools and external data sources. The researchers found that attackers can manipulate AI responses with surprising ease, and they propose a multi-layered defense strategy to protect against these threats.
explain_business: Prompt injection attacks pose substantial risk to deployed AI systems, with documented severe incidents like remote code execution vulnerabilities and credential theft. Minimal attack effort achieves high success rates, particularly when data sources are involved. Organizations implementing AI agents must adopt comprehensive, layered security approaches aligned with OWASP standards rather than relying on single defenses. This represents an ongoing architectural challenge requiring continuous monitoring and evolving protection strategies as threat vectors expand.
explain_practitioner: This comprehensive review analyzes prompt injection vulnerabilities in LLMs and agent systems from 2023-2025, examining 45 sources and real exploits. It categorizes attack vectors including direct jailbreaking, indirect injection via external content, tool poisoning through MCP, and RAG poisoning demonstrating 90% manipulation success with five documents. Critical incidents documented include CVE-2025-53773 (CVSS 9.6) and credential leakage. The authors propose PALADIN, a five-layer defense framework, and map mitigations to OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2025, identifying fundamental limitations requiring architectural rather than tactical solutions.
